Same emission bug as the action namespace: `Promise<any>` for a setter that resolves with no value, while the neighbouring setBadgeBackgroundColor is `Promise<void>`. Correct type is knowable and matched by chrome-types.

The Gecko schema entry is `"async": true, "parameters": []` and MDN says the promise "is fulfilled with no arguments", so `Promise<void>` is the knowable correct type. Same single upstream root cause as menus.refresh, tabs.warmup and the badge-text-color setters: the DT generator falls back to `Promise<any>` for async functions with no callback params.
Identical declaration from the same schema entry (`"async": true, "parameters": []`); MDN documents fulfilment with no arguments. Should be `Promise<void>`.

The Gecko schema declares unregister as `"async": true` with `"parameters": []`, and MDN's unregister page lists "Return value: None", so the resolution value is void and `Promise<any>` is the generator's fallback. Our `Promise<void>` is the documented type.

reason: Upstream already types `getContent` precisely as `{content: string, encoding: string}`; the only `any` is `setContent`'s error callback param, documented as "describes error otherwise", which is genuinely open-ended and which our override merely restates as `unknown`. The override also flattens the callback and Promise overloads into single signatures that claim a Promise is returned even when a callback is passed, which is a regression rather than a fix.

The Firefox override does not fix the `any` in `setContent`, it deletes getContent and setContent outright, and upstream already marks both optional and `@deprecated Unsupported on Firefox at this time`. The real purpose is aligning the Firefox member set with the Chrome arm so the merge does not emit two divergent interfaces.

All three members (frameURL, useContentScriptContext, contextSecurityOrigin) are `"unsupported": true` in Firefox's schema and upstream already marks each `@deprecated Unsupported on Firefox at this time`, matching BCD; emptying the interface is our choice, not an upstream error.

`preprocessorScript` is present in Firefox's own schema and upstream carries its schema-supplied deprecation string, so upstream is not inventing a member; at most it loses the separate "unsupported" wording, which is a cosmetic doc issue on a deprecated field.

Every `update` overload and `onClicked` is `"unsupported": true` in devtools_panels.json and upstream flags each `@deprecated Unsupported on Firefox at this time`; BCD agrees the whole Button type is unavailable in Firefox, so upstream documents reality rather than misstating it.

Upstream already declares all five members our override lists, including `show(): void` (@since Chrome 140); we only reorder and strip docs, with the paired Firefox override cut down to onShown/onHidden. Nothing upstream is wrong.

`createStatusBarButton` and `onSearch` are schema-flagged unsupported and upstream marks both `@deprecated Unsupported on Firefox at this time`, consistent with BCD; our override simply keeps only onShown/onHidden.

Upstream already has both the promise and callback overloads of setExpression and setObject; the real deltas are widening setObject's jsonObject to `JsonObject | string` and giving setPage a promise/callback form, both of which match the Firefox declaration in the same patch. This is a Chrome/Firefox merge, not a Chrome error.

Upstream correctly declares two createSidebarPane overloads (promise form and callback form); our override collapses them into one hybrid `(title, callback?) => Promise<ExtensionSidebarPane>`, which is the merger's callback-plus-promise artifact and is less accurate than upstream. The whole SourcesPanel is unavailable in Firefox and both of its members are `"unsupported": true` in the schema with matching `@deprecated Unsupported on Firefox` markers upstream; an empty interface on our side proves nothing about upstream.

Chrome and Firefox override strings are byte-identical.

The function is `"unsupported": true` in Firefox's schema (and absent per BCD) and upstream flags it deprecated; the `Promise<Resource>` shape comes straight from Mozilla's own `"async": "callback"` annotation, so it is a faithful transcription of the schema for an API Firefox does not implement, while our void+callback form is Chrome's.

reason: `Promise<any>` is the generator's faithful rendering of a Gecko schema entry that says `"async": true` with no described callback (proved by the sibling pair at 1029 `getBadgeBackgroundColor(): Promise<ColorArray>` versus 1038 `getBadgeTextColor(): Promise<any>`), so nothing in @types is wrong; `Promise<void>` is our guess with no cited source. Upstream really says `Promise<any>`, but only because the Gecko schema declares no callback; the doc comment specifies no resolved value. Our `Promise<void>` is an unverified assumption, not a fix to a demonstrable upstream error.
Identical to pause: nothing upstream or in BCD states the resolution type, so `Promise<void>` is our assumption. This is one schema-underspecification class, not a per-function type defect.
